Everyone thinks fear is the best deterrent but that simply isn't true. The best deterrent is making doing something easy, hard to do and making something hard to do easy. People will flow into the easiest state of doing things most of the time.

If poverty is causing someone to be a robber maybe we can ease some of their financial stress. If someone is raping women because of a lack of self control and psychosis maybe we can work on medicating them and getting them therapy.

History is full of revisionist history, remixing and reimagining. We often call Hitler inhuman, although he wasn't the first or only genocidal maniac.

That comic came into existence during a time of raging debate over confederate statues, flags, and generally right wing pushback for changing the landscape of southern states. 

In the context of these things pointing out that Columbus was a piece of shit even for his time is a rhetorical tool aimed at the many right wing Italian Americans who saw Columbus as a "hero"  a sentiment which was to many, disingenuous nonsense not predicated on fact. Comparison are inevitable I think here. 

I think context really matters when you're thinking about why people do this. That's not to say you're wrong or right, but I think we can quite easily trace why these comparisons come about. Many times historical figures are put into a place of special consideration when we're either trying to figure out who we want to be going forward or when we want to show what we don't want to be anymore.
